findings.message: The 'Consider optional enhancements' bullet in Next Steps names only a category ('optional patterns that give a early-mover opportunity in AI search') with no data anchor, specific element, or action drawn from this audit's findings. It could be copy-pasted unchanged into any web audit report.
findings.context: Next Steps > Recommended Actions, bullet 3: 'Consider optional enhancements: optional patterns that give a early-mover opportunity in AI search'

findings.message: Negation-pivot construction: 'While X may suggest Y, the audit reveals Z' pattern appears in the Executive Summary — 'That figure is more tractable than it first appears' is a concession-pivot that lifts a rhetorical move into formal voice rather than stating the affirmative directly. The report should simply state the corrective fact ('356 of 368 instances trace to 65 recurring template patterns, so a single corrective edit per pattern resolves every instance it governs') without the pivot setup.
findings.context: Executive Summary: 'That figure is more tractable than it first appears: 356 of those instances trace to 65 recurring template patterns, meaning a single corrective edit per pattern resolves every instance it governs.'

findings.message: The report states that 'Common Crawl (the archive underpinning most major LLM training datasets) prioritises HTML for its LLM-training subsets, so a plain-text llms.txt is unlikely to enter training corpora at the same rate as the rest of the site.' This is a specific empirical claim about Common Crawl's prioritisation behaviour for LLM-training subsets that does not appear in the audit facts and is not a well-known binary fact verifiable from public specification. It is an asserted industry behaviour presented as established fact without a citation or audit-data anchor.
findings.context: Section 'A note on llms.txt': 'Common Crawl (the archive underpinning most major LLM training datasets) prioritises HTML for its LLM-training subsets, so a plain-text llms.txt is unlikely to enter training corpora at the same rate as the rest of the site.'
